purpose: Teach: 公司/至上/共和党/政務次官/古来/有事/必至/参院

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、中国系企業の公司形態を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Sakura, you wrote your paper on Chinese corporate structures, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, observational opening. Gentle confirmation—not interrogation. Interested in what she chose. Steady eye contact, slight nod of recognition.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、近代国家の至上命令を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I focused on the imperative of the modern nation-state.
lines.style: Quiet confidence. Direct but not defensive. She's thought about this—let it land simply. No performance, just clarity.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 米国共和党の地域政策を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And you looked at regional policy under US Republicans?
lines.style: Thoughtful, gently curious. Not testing—genuinely tracing her interests. Slight lift of attention, waiting to hear where she went with it.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、戦後の政務次官制度を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, the postwar system of vice-ministers.
lines.style: Steady, assured. She's on solid ground here. No hesitation, but not rushed either. Direct handoff to the next point.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 古来の伝統行事を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And your third paper covered traditional ceremonies from antiquity?
lines.style: Leaning in slightly with genuine interest. Warm acknowledgment of range. The kind of question that shows she's paying attention to the whole picture.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、有事法制の議論史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I examined the legislative history around emergency law.
lines.style: Even, grounded. She's presenting her work plainly. A slight certainty underneath—she knows what she's done. No apology in the voice.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 選挙制度改革の必至性を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Your last one was on the inevitability of electoral reform?
lines.style: Reflective, inviting her to complete the arc. Not rushing. The kind of teacher who lets silence sit so students can think.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、参院選の地域別動向を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, regional voting trends in the Upper House elections.
lines.style: Clear, final. She's delivered her work. Slight sense of completion—not trailing off, but settling. Present and done.
